narrative:
The model determined that you have about a 30% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and the portion of your income that would go toward monthly payments. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk; only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation, while most (59%) have no checking account at all. This signaled higher risk to the model. The amount you asked for (2,462 DM) worked in your favor because it is noticeably below the average requested by approved applicants (about 3,020 DM), pulling the prediction toward approval. Similarly, the share of your income needed for installments (2%) was lower than the typical 3% seen among approved loans, which also helped reduce the risk score.

Even though two of the top factors spoke in your favor, the negative signal from your checking-account status was strong enough to outweigh them and tip the overall decision against approval.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account—bringing it out of the red and ideally building a positive balance—before reapplying. This single change would remove the biggest obstacle the model identified.
